name: CUT valuePreservationByRemoveLP pays compensation at the live PancakeSwap spot price
summary: CUT 0x7057f3b0f4d0649b428f0d8378a8a0e7d21d36a7 routes every transfer through the deal-type logic contract 0x7b2e7cb89824236cb7096cde7a153af30f3ecbaf, whose valuePreservationByRemoveLP(address,uint256) (selector 0x70f88861) tops up a liquidity remover with extra CUT so that the USDT value of the withdrawn position is preserved. It computes that top-up from a USDT-denominated pool value held in registry 0x0917914b0a70ee7f1f2460fcd487696856e31154 and converts it to CUT at the instantaneous reserve ratio of the PancakeSwap USDT/CUT pair 0x83681f67069a154815a0c6c2c97e2daca6ed3249, which it reads through token0(), token1() and getReserves() in the same call, with no averaging, deviation bound, or same-transaction guard. The conversion is therefore algebraically a constant times the pair's live CUT reserve: across all ten invocations inside the anchor transaction the excess paid over the amount passed in equals 0.283287608274 times the CUT reserve read in that same call, constant to twelve significant figures while the reserve grows from 757,225.933923 to 5,083,077.535048 CUT and the spot price falls from 2.3384 to 0.0538 USDT per CUT. The attacker exploits exactly that: inside one transaction it adds liquidity asymmetrically, dumps CUT into the pair to crush the price, and removes liquidity, so a fixed USDT obligation is settled in 4.54 times more CUT than it was worth, and the freshly issued CUT is sold back into the pair for the LPs' USDT. The violated invariant is that a payout denominated in one asset must not be converted at a price the payee can set in the same transaction. No parameter value restores it: an identical eth_call against the same deployed bytecode at block 42131696 returns the amount unchanged, and the defect is the unguarded spot conversion itself, not any configured value.
notes: The deal-type logic contract has no proxy and no upgrade path; its 16448-byte runtime is byte-identical at its creation block, immediately before the exploit and today.

Loss is the USDT the PancakeSwap USDT/CUT pair 0x83681f67069a154815a0c6c2c97e2daca6ed3249 lost to the campaign, summed over the USDT Transfer logs of the three exploit transactions: 1,271,656.254497 in 0x2c123d08..., 159,616.865472 in 0xce6e474d... and 8,290.512970 in 0x6262c0f1..., total 1,439,563.632938965392877836 USDT, against which the pair received 955,130,899.07835 CUT that the campaign itself created. That is the whole of the USDT that left the pair in those three transactions; 1,416,033.632938965392877836 reached the attacker's beneficiary 0x5766d1f03378f50c7c981c014ed5e5a8124f38a4 and 23,530 was the flash-swap fee retained by the funding pair 0x16b9a82891338f9ba80e2d6970fdda79d1eb0dae, and under the gross-depletion rule the fee is not deducted. No flash-loan principal is included: the loans are borrowed and repaid inside each transaction and net to zero at the lender. The pair's raw USDT balance falls further, from 1,454,183.768693 at block 42131696 to 1,419.854250 at block 42132019, but the extra 13,200.28 is ordinary third-party trading in the intervening blocks and is excluded. Binance-Peg BSC-USD is valued at par.

The deal-type logic contract is not source-verified on BscScan. Identity of the defective function and its dependence on the live pair reserves were established from the deployed bytecode's execution: the call trace of the anchor, an eth_call replay of the identical calldata against the same runtime at block 42131696, and the exact proportionality of the payout to the pair reserve read inside each call.

The campaign is three transactions in the same 322 blocks against the same defect; they are one incident with one loss, anchored on the first. realizedAt is not set because the last transaction is 967 seconds after the anchor and the loss is valued at par.
